speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To begin, can you describe exactly how your gait has changed and whether you experience any numbness, weakness, or vision changes alongside it?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the "drunken" gait suggests significant cerebellar involvement. Can you tell me if these symptoms appeared suddenly like a stroke, or did they develop gradually over weeks or months? Also, have you experienced any issues with your eyesight, such as double vision or trouble focusing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history is critical; natalizumab is strongly associated with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Have you noticed any new visual disturbances, such as blurred vision or blind spots, or any changes in your sense of touch?
